subject: p-fc
title: P.FC.------PHY.U.P.
description: Diagram in AE(PD)-16, third of three on book p128, paired with v2-p128-1 and v2-p128-2. Closes Braxton's triple-presentation: each schematic on this page holds the same activism question against a different crossing partner. (C)P-FC (the concept of point-focus) is crossed with PHY-U-P (physical universe particulars): the question is what point-focus produces when crossed with physical-universe-particulars — closing the activism-conditions argument by routing through physical-universe ground. PHY-U-P sits at the top. VT-DY (vibrational dynamics) and INFO-DS (information descent) form the upper-right cluster with RT-ALGN (reality alignment) on the right output. V-SY (vibrational system) and AF-NT (affinity-nature) anchor the right margin. INTR (interior) sits between subject and partner on the lower bridge. IST-F (interior-source functionalism) hangs below. AF-DY (affinity dynamics) and LANG (language) form the lower-left upstream chain. Structural argument: point-focus crossed with physical-universe-particulars is mediated by interior as central hub and interior-source-functionalism as lower support. The doubled lower upstreams (affinity-dynamics and language) expose the structural commitment: physical-universe-particulars can only produce reality-alignment when the language and affinity-dynamics paths converge through interior. The three diagrams on this page together comprise Braxton's argument that sixties activism's effective form was a *triple crossing* — composite-focus against principle-information (v2-p128-1), gradualism against information-dynamics (v2-p128-2), and point-focus against physical-universe-particulars (v2-p128-3) — and that the seventies' decline came from holding only one of these crossings at a time rather than all three.
